Summary: Course Definition & Identity Management
Description: Create and maintain the authoritative institutional course/programme record: identity, department ownership, classification, duration and mandatory metadata. Satisfies FR-01, FR-02, FR-03, BR-01–05, and the diagram's Key Business Rules panel.

Summary: Create a new draft course
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to create a new course/programme record with its mandatory identity and ownership data, so that a governed draft exists before it can be reviewed and published.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am an authenticated Academic Admin with Create permission, When I POST /api/v1/courses with courseCode, courseName, courseType, duration, totalCredits, departmentId, description, prerequisites and tags, Then a new course document is persisted with status=DRAFT and version="1.0", And a CourseCreated event is published, And the response returns id, courseCode, status, version and createdAt per the sample Create Course Response (Panel 6/7, FR-01).

Summary: Enforce scoped course-code uniqueness
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to enforce that courseCode is unique within an institution, so that duplicate course identities can never exist.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a courseCode already exists within the institution, When a create or code-change request is submitted with the same normalized code, Then the request is rejected with a 409 Conflict error per the Failure Handling table, and no document is written (BR-01, Panel 11/12).

Summary: Normalize course code before validation
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to normalize courseCode (case, whitespace, formatting) before uniqueness validation, so that cosmetically different codes cannot bypass duplicate detection.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a courseCode is submitted in any casing or with leading/trailing whitespace, When the create/update request is processed, Then the service normalizes the code prior to running the uniqueness check (BR-02).

Summary: Update a draft course
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to update the fields of a course that is still in DRAFT status, so that I can correct or refine details before submission for approval.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course is in status=DRAFT and I hold Update permission, When I PUT /api/v1/courses/{id} with changed fields, Then the fields are updated in place and version metadata is incremented, And attempting the same update once the course is ACTIVE requires the governed new-version path instead (API Design Panel 3, Key Business Rules Panel 11).

Summary: Validate department reference on course create/update
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to validate that departmentId resolves to a real, authorized department, so that courses are never associated with an invalid department.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a departmentId is supplied on create or update, When the service validates it against course_departments/Department reference data, Then the request succeeds only if the department exists and is active, otherwise a 400 Invalid department error is returned (Failure Handling Panel 12).

Summary: Enforce total credits greater than zero
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to require totalCredits to be a positive value, so that no course can be published with zero or negative credit value.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course draft has totalCredits <= 0, When a submit-for-approval or publish action is attempted, Then the action is rejected with a validation error, consistent with the rule 'Total credits must be greater than zero' (Key Business Rules Panel 11).

Summary: View course detail
Description: As an authorized user (Faculty, Student, Department Head, Admin), I want to retrieve the full detail of a specific course, so that I can review its current authoritative definition.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a valid course id and an authenticated user with view permission scoped appropriately, When GET /api/v1/courses/{id} is called, Then the current course document is returned with HTTP 200, scoped per the RBAC matrix in Panel 8.

Summary: Retrieve course credit information
Description: As Faculty, Student or Examination Module (EXM), I want to retrieve the total and component credit breakdown of a course, so that examination and evaluation calculations use the authoritative credit value.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course exists, When GET /api/v1/courses/{id}/credits is called, Then totalCredits and any credit breakdown are returned, sourced from the course and course_evaluation_policy collections (API Design Panel 3).

Summary: Support bulk import and export of course records
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to bulk import and export course records, so that I can migrate or synchronize large course catalogs efficiently during onboarding or data corrections.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a properly formatted bulk import file, When it is submitted via the bulk import endpoint, Then each row is validated against the same business rules as a single create (uniqueness, department, credits), row-level errors are reported without aborting the whole batch, and a bulk export produces an equivalent file of current course records (Responsibilities Panel 2).

Summary: Course Catalog & Search
Description: Provide indexed, filterable, paginated catalog search across courses, and maintain a published course_catalog projection so that students, faculty, admins and management can discover courses efficiently. Satisfies FR-09.

Summary: Search and filter courses
Description: As an authorized user, I want to search and filter courses by department, status, type and keyword with pagination, so that I can quickly find relevant courses in a large catalog.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I call GET /api/v1/courses/search with filter and pagination query parameters, When the request is processed, Then matching results are returned using indexed queries within the performance target, and only fields appropriate to my role are included (API Design Panel 3, FR-09).

Summary: Retrieve the published course catalog
Description: As a Student or external portal, I want to retrieve the published course catalog, so that I only see courses approved and released for public/institutional consumption.
Acceptance Criteria: Given one or more courses have been published to the catalog, When GET /api/v1/courses/catalog is called, Then only catalog-projected, published-course entries are returned from course_catalog, excluding DRAFT/REVIEW/deactivated courses (API Design Panel 3).

Summary: Maintain the course_catalog projection on publish/update
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to update the course_catalog projection whenever a course is published, updated, activated or deactivated, so that the public catalog view is always consistent with the authoritative course record.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course transitions status or its published fields change, When the change commits, Then the course_catalog document is synchronously or eventually updated to match, and a CourseCatalogUpdated event is emitted (MongoDB Collections Panel 4, Events Panel 9).

Summary: Restrict catalog visibility for students to active/published courses
Description: As a Student, I want catalog search and browse to return only published, active courses, so that I never see draft, suspended or archived programmes.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am authenticated as a Student, When I search or browse the catalog, Then only ACTIVE, catalog-visible courses are returned regardless of query filters, per the Student role's 'View published course catalog' permission (RBAC Panel 8).

Summary: Course Version & Lifecycle Management
Description: Create, publish and reconstruct immutable, point-in-time course versions, and govern effective-date integrity across versions. Satisfies FR-04, BR-06/07/13.

Summary: Create a new version on material change
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want a new version to be created whenever I make a material change to a published course, so that the previously published version remains untouched and historically accurate.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course has a currently ACTIVE/published version, When I submit a material change, Then a new course_versions document is created with an incremented version number and its own effectiveFrom date while the current version remains immutable, And a CourseVersionCreated event is emitted (BR-06, BR-13, Events Panel 9).

Summary: Publish a course version
Description: As an authorized approver, I want to publish a prepared course version, so that it becomes the effective, catalog-visible version for that course.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a version has passed validation, When I call POST /api/v1/courses/{id}/publish, Then the version's status becomes effective, the course status moves toward ACTIVE, the prior version is superseded, and a CourseVersionCreated/CoursePublished event pair is emitted per Panel 9 (API Design Panel 3).

Summary: Enforce non-overlapping effective dates across versions
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to reject a new version whose effectiveFrom/effectiveTo range overlaps an existing version's range, so that exactly one version is ever effective at any point in time.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an existing version is effective for a date range, When a new version is submitted with an overlapping effective date range, Then the request is rejected with a validation error, consistent with the rule 'Effective date must not overlap with existing version' (Key Business Rules Panel 11).

Summary: Require a new version for changes to a published course
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to block direct in-place edits to a course once it has a published/effective version, so that every material change after publication is captured as a new, auditable version.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course's current version is ACTIVE, When a caller attempts to directly mutate published fields instead of creating a new version, Then the operation is rejected, consistent with 'Changes to published course require new version' (Key Business Rules Panel 11).

Summary: Retrieve version history for a course
Description: As an authorized user, I want to list all versions of a course, so that I can review how the course definition has evolved over time.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course with one or more versions, When I call GET /api/v1/courses/{id}/versions, Then all versions are returned ordered by version number with status and effective dates (API Design Panel 3).

Summary: Prevent mutation of published versions
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to reject any attempt to modify a published course_versions document, so that historical reconstruction always remains trustworthy.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course_versions document has status=effective/published, When any update operation targets that document directly, Then the operation is rejected at the application and repository layer (BR-06).

Summary: Course Prerequisite Management
Description: Maintain the course-to-course prerequisite graph with cycle prevention, mandatory-flagging, and controlled growth. Satisfies FR-08, BR-09/10/11.

Summary: Add a course prerequisite
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to add a prerequisite relationship (with mandatory/optional flag) between two courses, so that eligibility rules can be enforced by downstream services.
Acceptance Criteria: Given both the source and prerequisite courses exist and are valid, When I POST /api/v1/courses/{id}/prerequisites with prerequisiteCourseId, type and mandatory flag, Then the relationship is validated for cycles and persisted, and a CoursePrerequisiteAdded event is emitted (API Design Panel 3, Events Panel 9).

Summary: Reject prerequisite cycles
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to detect and reject any prerequisite relationship that would create a cycle in the prerequisite graph, so that eligibility logic downstream never enters an unresolvable loop.
Acceptance Criteria: Given adding a proposed prerequisite edge would create a cycle in the directed prerequisite graph, When the add-prerequisite request is validated, Then the request is rejected and 'Prerequisites must be valid and active courses' is enforced (Key Business Rules Panel 11, BR-10).

Summary: Reject prerequisites referencing an invalid or inactive course
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to reject a prerequisite that references a course that does not exist or is not active, so that the graph never contains dangling or stale references.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a prerequisiteCourseId does not resolve to an active course, When the add-prerequisite request is validated, Then it is rejected with a 404 Not Found error per the Failure Handling table (Panel 12).

Summary: Remove a course prerequisite
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to remove an existing prerequisite relationship, so that I can correct or retire an obsolete eligibility rule.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an active prerequisite relationship exists, When I call DELETE /api/v1/courses/{id}/prerequisites/{prerequisiteId}, Then the relationship is removed/deactivated and a CoursePrerequisiteRemoved event is emitted (API Design Panel 3, Events Panel 9).

Summary: List prerequisites for a course
Description: As an authorized user, I want to view the full set of active prerequisites for a course, so that I understand its eligibility chain before enrollment or curriculum design.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course id, When I call GET /api/v1/courses/{id}/prerequisites, Then all active prerequisite relationships are returned via an indexed lookup.

Summary: Course–Department Association Management
Description: Maintain the dedicated course-to-department association collection so ownership, cross-department offerings and reassignment are governed independently of the core course record.

Summary: Associate a course with its owning department
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to record a course's owning department in a dedicated association collection, so that department ownership is queryable and auditable independent of the course master record.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course is created or its department changes, When the association is written, Then a course_departments document links courseId to departmentId with an effective date, matching the diagram's 'Department association' purpose (MongoDB Collections Panel 4).

Summary: Reassign a course to a different department
Description: As a Registrar, I want to reassign a course to a new owning department, so that organizational restructuring is reflected without losing the prior department history.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course currently belongs to Department A, When an authorized user reassigns it to Department B, Then a new course_departments record is created effective from the reassignment date while the prior association is retained for history, and only authorized roles (Registrar/Department Head with cross-department permission) may perform this action (RBAC Panel 8).

Summary: List all courses owned by a department
Description: As a Department Head, I want to list every course owned by my department, so that I can manage my department's academic catalog.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I am a Department Head, When I query courses scoped to my department, Then only courses associated with my departmentId in course_departments are returned, consistent with the 'Manage department courses' permission (RBAC Panel 8).

Summary: Course Accreditation & Regulatory Compliance
Description: Maintain accreditation and regulatory-body details (UGC, AICTE, NBA, NAAC, etc.) per course, so accreditation status is governed, auditable and mandatory for regulatory courses. Ties to the Key Business Rule that accreditation details are mandatory for regulatory courses.

Summary: Record accreditation details for a course
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to record accreditation/regulatory details (authority, reference number, validity dates) for a course, so that regulatory compliance is documented against the authoritative course record.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course requires regulatory accreditation, When I submit accreditation details (authority, reference, validFrom/validTo), Then a course_accreditation document is created and linked to the course, matching 'Accreditation & regulatory details' (MongoDB Collections Panel 4).

Summary: Enforce mandatory accreditation for regulatory course categories
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to require at least one valid accreditation record before publishing a course flagged as regulatory (e.g. UGC/AICTE-governed programmes), so that non-compliant courses cannot become effective.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course is classified as a regulatory category, When a publish action is attempted without an associated valid course_accreditation record, Then publication is blocked with a validation error, consistent with 'Accreditation details mandatory for regulatory courses' (Key Business Rules Panel 11).

Summary: Alert on expiring accreditation
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to be alerted when a course's accreditation validity is approaching expiry, so that renewal can be initiated before the course falls out of compliance.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course_accreditation record's validTo date is within the configured lead-time window, When the monitoring check runs, Then a notification is raised to the accountable Academic Admin/Department Head.

Summary: Curriculum & Subject Cross-Module Mapping
Description: Maintain course-to-curriculum and course-to-subject linkage collections that let ACD-01 expose structural context to ACD-02 (Curriculum) and ACD-03 (Subjects) without owning their data. Cross-module integration per Panel 10.

Summary: Link a course to its curriculum reference
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to maintain a course_curriculum_map entry linking a course to its ACD-02 curriculum identity, so that curriculum structure can be resolved from course context via REST + events without ACD-01 owning curriculum data.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course is linked to a curriculum defined in ACD-02, When the mapping is created or updated, Then a course_curriculum_map document records the reference by identifier only, consistent with 'Provide course structure' (Cross-Module Integration Panel 10).

Summary: Map subjects to a course
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to maintain a course_subjects mapping reflecting which ACD-03 subjects belong to a course, so that ACD-03 and other consumers can resolve course-subject structure via REST + events.
Acceptance Criteria: Given ACD-03 publishes or the admin records subject-to-course associations, When the mapping is synchronized, Then course_subjects reflects the current subject set for the course, matching 'Map subjects to course' (Cross-Module Integration Panel 10, MongoDB Collections Panel 4).

Summary: Expose course structure to Curriculum and Subject modules via API/events
Description: As ACD-02 (Curriculum) or ACD-03 (Subjects), I want to query or subscribe to course structural context from ACD-01, so that my module stays consistent with the authoritative course definition without direct database access.
Acceptance Criteria: Given ACD-02/ACD-03 need course structural context, When they call the relevant REST endpoints or consume ACD-01's domain events, Then they receive course/curriculum/subject linkage data consistent with the Cross-Module Integration table (Panel 10), and never query ACD-01's database directly.

Summary: Course Batch Offerings Management
Description: Track which batches/sections (ACD-04) offer a given course, and enforce lifecycle rules that depend on active batch offerings. Satisfies 'Course offerings per batch' integration and the deactivation-gating business rule.

Summary: Record a course-batch offering
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to record that a course is being offered to a specific batch/section, so that ACD-04 and downstream services can resolve which batches run which courses.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a batch defined in ACD-04 offers a course, When the offering is recorded, Then a course_batch_offerings document links courseId, batchId and the offering term, matching 'Batch-wise course offerings' (MongoDB Collections Panel 4).

Summary: Block course deactivation while active batch offerings exist
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to block deactivation of a course that still has active batch offerings, so that in-progress academic delivery is never silently orphaned.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course has one or more active entries in course_batch_offerings, When a deactivate action is attempted, Then it is rejected with a validation error, consistent with 'Course deactivation allowed only if no active batches' (Key Business Rules Panel 11).

Summary: List batch offerings for a course
Description: As an Academic Admin or Faculty, I want to list all batches currently offering a course, so that I can understand its delivery footprint before making lifecycle or curriculum decisions.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course id, When I query its batch offerings, Then all current and historical course_batch_offerings entries are returned, indexed by courseId.

Summary: Course Attendance & Evaluation Policy Management
Description: Maintain per-course attendance rules and evaluation/credit rules as dedicated governed collections, so ACD-06 (Attendance) and EXM (Examination) can consume authoritative, versioned policy context. Satisfies the total-credits business rule and course_attendance_policy/course_evaluation_policy purposes.

Summary: Define an attendance policy for a course
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to define the minimum attendance percentage and related rules for a course, so that the Attendance module can enforce eligibility consistently.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course requires a specific attendance rule, When I submit a minimum attendance percentage and any exceptions, Then a course_attendance_policy document is created/updated and linked to the course, matching 'Attendance rules per course' (MongoDB Collections Panel 4).

Summary: Define an evaluation/credit policy for a course
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to define evaluation weightage and credit-distribution rules for a course, so that grading and credit calculations are governed by an authoritative, versioned policy.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course's evaluation structure is being defined, When I submit component weightages (internal/external) and credit distribution, Then a course_evaluation_policy document is created/updated and the total resolves to the course's totalCredits, matching 'Evaluation/credit rules' (MongoDB Collections Panel 4, Key Business Rules Panel 11).

Summary: Expose attendance and evaluation policy to ACD-06/EXM via API
Description: As the Attendance module (ACD-06) or Examination module (EXM), I want to read a course's attendance and evaluation policy through ACD-01's API, so that my module enforces rules consistent with the authoritative course definition.
Acceptance Criteria: Given ACD-06 or EXM needs a course's policy, When they call the relevant read endpoint, Then the current effective attendance/evaluation policy is returned, versioned consistently with the course's current version.

Summary: Course Document Management
Description: Store and govern brochures, regulations, syllabi and other course-related documents as metadata references linked to a course. Satisfies 'Course document management' key feature and course_documents purpose.

Summary: Attach a document to a course
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to attach a brochure, regulation or syllabus document to a course, so that supporting materials are discoverable alongside the authoritative course record.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a document has been uploaded to the platform's document/object storage, When I link it to a course, Then a course_documents record is created referencing the document by identifier/URL, document type and version, matching 'Brochures, regulations, syllabi' (MongoDB Collections Panel 4). Actual file bytes are never embedded in MongoDB.

Summary: List and retrieve documents for a course
Description: As a Student or Faculty, I want to list and download the documents associated with a course, so that I can access the syllabus, brochure or regulation I need.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course has one or more linked documents, When I query them, Then metadata (title, type, version, link) is returned, filtered by my role's visibility (public brochure vs internal regulation).

Summary: Replace or version a course document
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to upload a new version of a course document (e.g. updated syllabus), so that the latest official version is always available while prior versions remain traceable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a document already exists for a course, When I upload a replacement, Then a new course_documents version entry is created and marked current, while the prior entry is retained for audit.

Summary: Course Tags & Categorization
Description: Maintain a dedicated tags/keywords collection per course to power discovery, categorization and search relevance. Satisfies 'Tags, categories and keywords' purpose.

Summary: Add tags/keywords to a course
Description: As an Academic Admin, I want to add tags and keywords to a course, so that it can be discovered more easily through search and categorization.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course exists, When I add one or more tags (e.g. "UG", "APPLICATIONS"), Then a course_tags document is created/updated linking the tags to the course, matching the sample Create Course Request's tags array (Panel 7, MongoDB Collections Panel 4).

Summary: Search courses by tag/keyword
Description: As an authorized user, I want to search courses by tag or keyword, so that I can find courses within a thematic or categorical grouping rather than by exact code/name.
Acceptance Criteria: Given courses have been tagged, When I search using a tag filter, Then matching courses are returned via an index on course_tags.

Summary: Course Archive Management
Description: Move retired/archived courses into a dedicated archive collection while retaining them for audit and reporting, distinct from active in-place status flags. Satisfies 'Archived/retired courses' purpose and the soft-delete business rule.

Summary: Archive a retired course into course_archive
Description: As an Authorized Admin, I want a deactivated/retired course to be projected into a dedicated course_archive collection, so that archived courses are retained for audit and reporting without cluttering active operational queries.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course transitions to an archived/retired status, When the archive action completes, Then a course_archive record is created (or the course is soft-deleted and flagged) with a reference back to its final version and history, matching 'Archived/retired courses' (MongoDB Collections Panel 4) and 'Soft delete - retain for audit and reporting' (Key Business Rules Panel 11).

Summary: Query archived/retired courses for audit and reporting
Description: As an Auditor, I want to query course_archive independently of the active course catalog, so that I can produce historical/compliance reports without impacting live operational queries.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I hold the Auditor role, When I query course_archive, Then all archived/retired course records are returned with their final state and links to course_history, consistent with the Auditor's 'View course history and changes' permission (RBAC Panel 8).

Summary: Course Lifecycle Governance
Description: Govern the full course lifecycle state machine — activate, suspend, deactivate, soft-delete/archive — without ever deleting historical evidence. Satisfies FR-07, BR-08.

Summary: Update course lifecycle status
Description: As an Authorized Admin, I want to transition a course's status (draft, active, deactivated, etc.) through a single governed endpoint, so that every lifecycle change is validated and audited consistently.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a requested status transition, When I call PUT /api/v1/courses/{id}/status, Then the transition is validated against the allowed state machine, the status is updated, and the change is recorded in course_history (API Design Panel 3).

Summary: Reject invalid lifecycle transitions
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to validate every lifecycle transition against the domain state machine, so that illegal transitions can never occur.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a requested transition is not permitted from the course's current status, When the transition action is invoked, Then the request is rejected with a 400 Business rule violation error per the Failure Handling table, and the course status remains unchanged (Panel 12).

Summary: Retrieve change history for a course
Description: As an authorized user or Auditor, I want to retrieve the full change history for a course, so that I can review every lifecycle transition, update and who performed it.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course has one or more history entries, When I call GET /api/v1/courses/{id}/history, Then all course_history entries are returned in chronological order with actor and timestamp (API Design Panel 3, RBAC Panel 8).

Summary: Event-Driven Integration
Description: Reliably publish the full ACD-01 domain event catalog (CourseCreated, CourseUpdated, CourseActivated, CourseDeactivated, CourseVersionCreated, CoursePrerequisiteAdded, CoursePrerequisiteRemoved, CourseCatalogUpdated) and consume upstream events, so downstream modules stay eventually consistent. Satisfies FR-10 and Events Panel 9.

Summary: Publish the full ACD-01 domain event catalog via transactional outbox
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want every state-changing operation to write its corresponding domain event (CourseCreated, CourseUpdated, CourseActivated, CourseDeactivated, CourseVersionCreated, CoursePrerequisiteAdded, CoursePrerequisiteRemoved, CourseCatalogUpdated) to a transactional outbox, so that events are never lost even if the broker is temporarily unavailable.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course create/update/activate/deactivate/version/prerequisite/catalog operation commits successfully, When the transaction completes, Then the corresponding event from the Events catalog (Panel 9) is durably recorded in outbox_events within the same transaction and relayed to Kafka/RabbitMQ with retry until acknowledged.

Summary: Notify stakeholders on course creation
Description: As a Notification Service consumer, I want to receive a notification trigger when a course is successfully created, so that relevant stakeholders (department, approvers) are informed without polling.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course is created, When the CourseCreated event is published, Then the Notification Service sends the configured stakeholder notification, matching Step 6 of the Create Course sequence diagram (Panel 6).

Summary: Deduplicate inbound events using event identity
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want to deduplicate inbound events, so that redelivered or replayed events never cause duplicate side effects.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an inbound event has already been processed successfully, When it is redelivered, Then the service recognizes the duplicate and skips reprocessing without error.

Summary: Route unprocessable events to a dead-letter queue
Description: As a Platform Operator, I want events that repeatedly fail processing to be routed to a dead-letter queue after retries are exhausted, so that they can be investigated and replayed without blocking the main stream.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an inbound or outbound event fails processing after the maximum configured retry attempts, When retries are exhausted, Then the event is persisted to dead_letter_events with failure context and an alert is raised, consistent with 'Event publishing failure -> retry with backoff' then store-in-outbox/retry-async (Failure Handling Panel 12).

Summary: Guarantee exactly-once processing of retried academic commands
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want retried commands and mutation requests deduplicated via idempotency records, so that repeated client or gateway retries never apply a business effect twice.
Acceptance Criteria: Given an idempotencyKey and operation, when the same key is replayed with an identical request hash, then the original responseRef is returned without reapplying the operation | Given the same idempotencyKey is replayed with a mismatched request hash, then the request is rejected as a conflicting duplicate | Given expiresAt passes, then the idempotency record is eligible for cleanup without affecting already-completed operations (MongoDB Collections Panel 4, Reliability Panel 12).

Summary: Security, RBAC & Audit Governance
Description: Enforce the full role-based access matrix (System Admin, Academic Admin, Department Head, Faculty, Student, Auditor, External API), classify data sensitivity, and maintain an immutable audit trail. Satisfies FR-12/13 and RBAC Panel 8.

Summary: Enforce the full 7-role RBAC permission matrix
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want every endpoint to check the caller's role against the RBAC matrix (System Admin: all permissions; Academic Admin: create/update/publish/deactivate; Department Head: manage department courses; Faculty: view assigned department courses; Student: view published catalog; Auditor: view course history and changes; External API: read-only as per scope), so that only authorized actors can perform each action.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a user attempts an action without the corresponding permission for their role, When the request reaches the service, Then it is rejected with a 401/403 error per the Failure Handling table before any business logic executes, and the full matrix in RBAC Panel 8 is enforced consistently across every endpoint in the API Design panel.

Summary: Grant Auditor read-only access to course history and changes
Description: As an Auditor, I want read-only access to course history and change records across all courses, so that I can perform compliance reviews without any ability to modify data.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I hold the Auditor role, When I access any course_history, course_versions or course_archive endpoint, Then I receive read-only results and any write attempt is rejected, matching 'View course history and changes' (RBAC Panel 8).

Summary: Grant External API consumers scoped read-only access
Description: As an External API consumer (partner system or public integration), I want read-only access limited to the scope defined for my API key, so that I can consume published course data without any write capability or over-broad visibility.
Acceptance Criteria: Given I authenticate as an External API client, When I call any ACD-01 endpoint, Then I receive only the data within my granted scope and read-only access, matching 'Read-only access (as per scope)' (RBAC Panel 8).

Summary: Record an immutable, append-only history entry for every material change
Description: As a Compliance Officer, I want every lifecycle transition, publication and correction to be recorded as an append-only entry in course_history, so that a complete, tamper-evident audit trail always exists.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any material mutation occurs (create, update, submit, publish, activate, deactivate, prerequisite change, catalog update), When the mutation commits, Then a corresponding course_history record is written capturing action, actorId and timestamp, and history records can never be updated or deleted (MongoDB Collections Panel 4).

Summary: Attribute every material mutation to an authenticated actor
Description: As the Course Management Service, I want every material write to capture the authenticated actorId, so that all changes are individually attributable for audit and compliance.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any material mutation request, When it is processed, Then the actorId from the authenticated identity token is persisted alongside the change (matching "createdBy": "admin123" in the sample response, Panel 7).

Summary: Reject unauthorized and forbidden requests with the correct error codes
Description: As an API Consumer, I want unauthorized and forbidden actions to return the documented 401/403 error codes, so that I can build reliable client-side auth-error handling.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a request is unauthenticated or authenticated but lacking permission, When it is processed, Then it returns 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden respectively, exactly as documented in the Failure Handling table (Panel 12).

Summary: API Standards, Error Handling & Contracts
Description: Deliver a consistent, versioned REST contract with standardized request/response shapes and the full documented error taxonomy across every ACD-01 endpoint listed in the API Design panel.

Summary: Publish and version the ACD-01 API contract
Description: As an API Consumer, I want a versioned specification covering every /api/v1/courses endpoint (create, list, detail, update, delete/deactivate, publish, versions, prerequisites add/remove, search, catalog, status, history, credits), so that I can integrate against a stable, documented contract.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the ACD-01 service, When the API contract is published, Then it documents all endpoints listed in the API Design panel (Panel 3) with methods, paths and descriptions, and breaking changes require a new version.

Summary: Return standardized success and error response shapes
Description: As an API Consumer, I want every response to follow the standard {success, data} / {success:false, error} envelope, so that clients can handle responses uniformly.
Acceptance Criteria: Given any ACD-01 API call, When the response is returned, Then it conforms to the sample Create Course Response envelope shown in Panel 7.

Summary: Map every documented failure scenario to its specified error code
Description: As an API Consumer, I want every failure condition (duplicate course code, invalid department, prerequisite not found, business rule violation, database error, event publishing failure, unauthorized access, forbidden action, service unavailable) mapped to its documented HTTP status, so that I can build reliable client-side error handling.
Acceptance Criteria: Given each documented failure condition occurs, When the API responds, Then it returns exactly the status defined in the Failure Handling table (Panel 12): 409 duplicate code, 400 invalid department, 404 prerequisite not found, 400 business rule violation, 500 database error, retry-with-backoff for event publishing failure, 401 unauthorized, 403 forbidden, 503 service unavailable.

Summary: End-to-End Scenarios & Cross-Module Integration
Description: Validate complete cross-cutting flows spanning creation, publication, prerequisite management, batch offerings and every listed downstream module integration (ACD-02 through ACD-10, STM, HRM, EXM, COM). Satisfies End-to-End Architecture Panel 13 and Cross-Module Integration Panel 10.

Summary: E2E: Create → Validate → Persist → Notify (full sequence)
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test that mirrors the Create Course sequence diagram (Admin -> Gateway -> ACD-01 -> MongoDB -> Event Bus -> Notification Service), so that the full request path is proven end-to-end exactly as designed.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course creation request from the Admin Portal, When it flows through the API Gateway, ACD-01's validate/authorize/apply-business-rules/save steps, and the resulting event/notification fan-out, Then the response matches the documented 201 Created success response, and the Notification Service is confirmed to have sent the stakeholder notification (Sequence Diagram Panel 6).

Summary: E2E: verify each cross-module integration contract
Description: As a Release Manager, I want an end-to-end integration test per row of the Cross-Module Integration table (Curriculum, Subjects, Batches, Timetable, Student, Examination, HRM, Communication, Reporting), so that ACD-01 is not released until every downstream contract is proven.
Acceptance Criteria: Given the ACD-01 release candidate, When the full integration suite runs against ACD-02, ACD-03, ACD-04, ACD-05, STM, EXM, HRM, COM and ACD-10 Reporting, Then every REST + Events integration listed in Panel 10 is validated, and this gate is required before the service is marked production-ready.

Summary: E2E: deactivation blocked by active batches, then succeeds after batch closure
Description: As a QA Engineer, I want an end-to-end test proving a course cannot be deactivated while it has active batch offerings, and succeeds once those offerings close, so that the cross-collection business rule between course_batch_offerings and courses is continuously verified.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a course has an active course_batch_offerings entry, When deactivation is attempted, then rejected, and then re-attempted after the batch offering is closed, Then the first attempt fails per the business rule and the second succeeds with status updated and history recorded.
